summary: Design realistic cyber tabletop exercises, MSELs, and after-action plans. Build stronger incident readiness in 5 days.
lede: Cyber incident response tabletop exercise design helps security and risk professionals test how teams would handle a simulated incident. They learn to define scope and scenarios, sequence injects, facilitate decisions and escalation, and capture evidence in decision logs. They also map stakeholder notifications and turn observations into assigned remediation actions and after-action improvement plans.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to design, facilitate, and report cyber incident response tabletop exercises that reflect real operational risk, response roles, and improvement tracking. Cyber Incident Response Analysts who draft scenarios and injects. SOC Analysts who validate detection and escalation paths. Incident Response Managers who coordinate exercise scope and facilitation. Cybersecurity Governance Leads who align exercises with policy expectations. IT Risk Managers who track gaps and remediation actions. Security Operations Managers who oversee exercise logistics and readiness. Crisis Communications Managers who test breach communication pathways. Cloud Security Engineers who validate incident paths in cloud services. Business Continuity Coordinators who map response dependencies and recovery handoffs. External MSSP Liaison Managers who coordinate third-party response responsibilities.
prerequisites: Participants should have a working knowledge of incident response concepts, security operations workflows, and basic stakeholder communication during cyber events. Familiarity with incident handling terminology, risk registers, and internal reporting processes will help, but no coding or programming is required. Prior exposure to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework or NIST SP 800-61 is helpful, though the course will introduce the planning and design logic in a practical way.
